svg.title: Browser integration — okfy architecture explainer
svg.desc: How okfy, one HTML document with inline CSS and JavaScript, runs inside the browser. The page uses DOM and CSS, Canvas 2D with requestAnimationFrame and inline SVG to draw; the History API, popstate, beforeunload and pageshow to navigate and guard the page; localStorage, sessionStorage and URLSearchParams to remember; a service worker, the Cache API and a web app manifest to install and run offline; a Content-Security-Policy, URL containment and bounded streams to enforce its rules; the Fetch API, ReadableStream and AbortController to read a served bundle; the File System Access API, a directory input, File and Blob plus drag-and-drop to read a folder chosen from disk; TextDecoder, TextEncoder, DecompressionStream and blob URLs to decode; Web Audio, HTML media elements, getUserMedia and an AnalyserNode to play and analyse media; and Intl, matchMedia, devicePixelRatio and navigator values to follow the device. A served bundle is fetched same-origin, with no credentials and no redirects, and never leaves its origin. A local folder is read in place and never uploaded. A preview file is read only when opened. The service worker caches only the app shell, never bundle bytes. The optional, unreleased assistant is the one path off the page: when configured and asked, it may POST to an LLM provider over https or loopback http, list models, call a speech endpoint, open a realtime transcription WebSocket over wss or loopback ws, or redirect for OAuth, all gated by the policy's connect-src. Input comes from pointer and mouse, touch, the wheel, the keyboard, a context menu, a folder drag-and-drop, a folder picker and the microphone; output goes to the canvas, the DOM, Web Audio, media elements, synthesized speech and an installed standalone window. Chosen files do not leave the page, and there is no analytics, telemetry, CDN, external font or external image.
svg.text: How one HTML document runs inside the browser — features, files, network and devices
no build · no server · no SDK
One document; every capability is a browser API.
BROWSER — desktop, mobile or installed PWA
one HTML document · inline CSS + JavaScript
No framework · no build · no SDK
one IIFE · one <script> · no external code
The page is the runtime: no process, no install, no server-side application.
Grouped by what the page asks the browser to do.
Each route has its own reader, its own limits and the same rule: chosen files are never uploaded.
the page root is the bundle
only when a node is opened
or a File list from a drop
Markdown at open, files on click
never uploaded · no auto-load on file://
No file chosen from disk is uploaded. A served bundle stays on its origin.
Bundle traffic stays same-origin. Only the assistant, when configured and asked, leaves the page.
bundle root — Markdown, images, media, VTT
app shell — service-worker cache, never bundle bytes
The fence is checked on the URL and again on the response.
POST https, or http on loopback
Nothing is sent until you ask.
The service worker caches only the app shell; bundle bytes are never stored or intercepted.
Pointer, touch, keyboard, a folder drop and the microphone on one side; canvas, DOM, media and speech on the other.
AudioContext resumes on a user gesture.
Hover, width and reduced motion follow matchMedia.
prompt + tool results to the provider
realtime audio to the speech provider
No analytics, no telemetry, no CDN, no external fonts or images.
Assistant features are unreleased in this revision.
Source: okfy.html, okfy-sw.js, site.webmanifest and the project documentation.
